summary: Unexpected routing changes when data-location checks return slow — path selection and latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that after enabling strict data-location checks for their dedicated tenant, a subset of requests from their us-east clients were routed to eu-west endpoints and experienced 150–400ms additional tail latency. Impact: Several storefront features that do synchronous generation (product summary and inventory lookups) saw increased error rates and timeouts for ~2 hours. Timeline: 2024-11-05 09:12 UTC - first alert from Horizon Retail monitoring; 09:18 UTC - support ticket opened; 09:25 UTC - Support observed routing to eu-west for tokens originating in us-east; 10:00 UTC - engineering triage began. Environment: Dedicated cluster for Horizon Retail (tenant id: hr-023), strict data-location flag enabled at tenant level, autoscaling enabled. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use Horizon Retail API key and send a mix of short generation requests pinned to "us-east" residency with strict residency checks enabled; 2) Observe request trace headers (X-Redwood-Route, X-Residency-Check) and latency; 3) Reproduce at high QPS (~30 RPS) to see path selection differences. Observed behavior: Intermittent routing decision where the residency check RPC to the control plane timed out (client-side 120ms), causing the router to fall back to region-preference heuristics that picked eu-west endpoints (shortest available capacity) instead of honoring strict local enforcement. This fallback increased median P95 token latency by ~220ms and produced a small number of 504s. Expected behavior: With strict data-location checks enabled tenant traffic should either stay in-region or fail fast with a clear residency violation; it should not fall back to another region silently. Logs/traces: Traces attached below show X-Residency-Check=timeout and fallback_reason=control_plane_timeout. See trace IDs: hr-20241105-09-01, hr-20241105-09-14 (linked in comments). Temporary workaround: Disabled strict residency flag for the tenant at 11:05 UTC which restored in-region routing; engineering recommended this as a short-term mitigation while investigation proceeds.
comments: 2024-11-05 09:30 - Support (Aisha Kumar): Collected initial traces from customer and asked for a HAR of failing requests; asked SRE to pull router logs for hr-023.

2024-11-05 09:55 - SRE (Lena Price): Found control-plane residency-check RPC latencies spiking to 180ms for a small % of calls coming from the us-east fleet; router config had fallback policy set to 'prefer-capacity' which can route cross-region when check fails.

2024-11-05 10:10 - Eng (Tomas Ortega): Confirmed that a recent config change to reduce residency-check RPC timeout from 200ms to 120ms went out on 2024-11-04; rolling back timeout to 250ms recommended for stability.
2024-11-05 11:10 - Support (Aisha Kumar): Customer accepted temporary rollback of strict flag; customer reports reduced errors after rollback; asked for timeline for root cause fix.

2024-11-06 14:22 - Eng (Tomas Ortega): Implemented feature flag to make fallback behavior explicit in logs and return header X-Residency-Fallback-Policy; preparing PR to update default router behavior for strict residency tenants.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Recent timeout reduction for residency-check RPC made control-plane checks brittle under transient load spikes. 2) Fallback routing policy 'prefer-capacity' is too permissive for tenants with strict residency expectations. Findings: - Router logs show repeated 'residency_check_timeout' events correlated with peaks in control-plane CPU steal on us-east control-plane instances. - Metric: residency_check_success_rate dropped from 99.9% to 98.1% during the incident window. - No evidence of DNS/TLS issues between edge and eu-west; routing decision occurred server-side in gateway. Actions taken: - Rolled residency-check timeout back to 250ms in canary and validated recovery on canary gateways. - Added additional observability: residency check latency histogram and explicit fallback headers. - Drafted change to router default: for tenants with 'strict' residency, fallback should be 'fail_fast' unless an override is configured. Related artifacts: Slack thread #support-hr-023 (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02SUP123), PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2214.
resolution: Short-term: Reverted residency-check timeout to 250ms across us-east gateways (rolled 100% by 2024-11-06 03:00 UTC) and recommended Horizon Retail re-enable strict residency after 24h observation. Long-term: Change proposal merged to require explicit fallback override for strict-residency tenants and to surface fallback events as headers and in Console alerts. Follow-ups: - ENG-2876: update router docs and residency runbook; - OPS-512: increase control-plane capacity in us-east during peak windows. Customer communication: Sent status update and proposed timeline to Horizon Retail on 2024-11-06 09:30 UTC; customer accepted plan and marked ticket to be notified when changes are in prod.
